cases.title: The notes can't be read: one sentence about it, then a first lesson, nothing said before the snapshot

rubric.reason: Nothing is said before the first snapshot call; the mentor opens with one plain sentence, "I couldn't read my notes from your earlier lessons," names no file, field or error code, then proposes Title and starts a first lesson with the land-hard question.

Every layer, property and time the mentor mentions (Title Position 0.5–1.5, 1.5–3, 3–4.37 s, Scale 0.5–1.5 s, Old Take, CTRL, Icon, Logo's Rotation, Subtitle's Opacity, Bar's X Position, Glow's Blurriness) appears in the snapshot result.
The mentor makes no claim about the learner's earlier work; "still need easing" describes comp pairs from the tool's ease_first list, not whether the learner has learned easing.

After the snapshot, the mentor states the notes problem once in plain words ("I couldn't read my notes from your earlier lessons. They're kept as they were..."), names no file, field or code, and goes straight into a first lesson proposing Title.

Every name and time matches the snapshot: Title's Position 0.5 to 1.5 s, 1.5 to 3 s and 3 to 4.37 s, Scale 0.5 to 1.5 s, Old Take, CTRL, Icon, Logo's Rotation, Subtitle's Opacity, Bar's X Position and Glow's Blurriness.

The mentor says nothing about what the learner has or hasn't learned; "That belongs to the easing lesson" describes the comp's pairs, and the second snapshot's learned:false is never voiced as "you haven't learned easing".

The mentor said nothing before the snapshot, then opened once with the plain-words line "I couldn't read my notes from your earlier lessons...", named no file, field or error code, and went on to a first lesson on Title.

Every name and time matches the snapshot: Title's Position at 0.5 to 1.5 s, 1.5 to 3 s and 3 to 4.37 s (4.367 rounded), Title's Scale at 0.5 to 1.5 s, Old Take, CTRL, Icon, Logo's Rotation, Subtitle's Opacity, Bar's X Position and Glow's Blurriness.
The mentor makes no claim about the learner's earlier work; "still need easing. That's the easing lesson" describes comp pairs from the ease_first leave-outs, not the learner's history.
